6.1.intro: Before any ad, know your numbers. Then every choice is a simple comparison.

steps.say: Open the **Dashboard**, pick **Month**. Copy three numbers: target MER, break-even ROAS and break-even CPA.
steps.check: Three numbers are on your campaign brief.
steps.lost: Copy three numbers from the Dashboard.

steps.say: Work out your target cost per sale: average order × target MER. For ads to strangers, you can allow up to double that.
steps.check: You have a target CPA and a stranger CPA limit.
steps.lost: Average order × target MER. Then double it for stranger ads.

steps.say: Compare your target CPA with what similar stores pay for a customer. Yours is lower? Don't spend yet. Fix the offer, order size or margins first (Module 2).
steps.check: You know if your numbers can support ads today.
steps.careful: Only pay more for a first order if you have real proof people buy again, and what that second order earns.
steps.lost: Is your target CPA too small? Then fix the offer before ads.

6.2.intro: Each campaign has one job. The job decides what you pick in Ads Manager.

steps.say: Pick your campaign's job from the lesson table. For example: "Find new buyers".
steps.check: One job is on the brief.
steps.lost: Write: "Find new buyers".

steps.say:
Make the campaign.

1. In Ads Manager, click **+ Create**.
2. Choose the goal for this job. For new buyers: **Sales**.
3. In the ad set, set what it aims for. For new buyers: **Purchase**.
steps.check: The goal and event match the table.
steps.careful: Meta usually needs about 50 results a week to finish learning. Aim for a step that happens at least 25 to 50 times a week.
steps.lost: Click **+ Create**, choose **Sales**, then **Purchase**.

6.3.intro: Keep testing apart from winning, so new tests don't upset what works.

steps.say: Make a **build campaign** that's always switched off. Build each new ad there once.
steps.check: A paused campaign holds every ad you've made.
steps.lost: Make one campaign. Keep it off. Store ads there.

steps.say: Make a **testing campaign** with 20 to 30% of your budget. Put each new batch of ads there.
steps.check: New ads get a fair budget away from winners.
steps.lost: One test campaign. About a quarter of your budget.

steps.say: Keep proven ads in **scaling campaigns** with 70 to 80% of your budget. Don't add new ads while they're winning.
steps.check: Scaling campaigns stay steady.
steps.lost: Winners stay put. Don't poke them.

steps.say: When a test ad wins, copy it into scaling using **Use existing post**, so it keeps its likes and comments.
steps.check: The winner runs with its likes intact.
steps.lost: Move winners with **Use existing post**.

6.4.intro: How many campaigns you need depends on how much you spend. Too many, and each one starves.

steps.say: Find your daily spend in the lesson table. Set up the campaigns it lists.
steps.check: Your account fits your budget.
steps.lost: Small budget? Fewer campaigns. That's the rule.

steps.say: Split your budget. Small: 70 to 80% strangers, 20 to 30% people who know you. Later: strangers 30 to 50%, mixed 30 to 40%, warm 20 to 30%.
steps.check: Each audience gets its share.
steps.lost: Start with most money on strangers.

steps.say: When results are steady, test one other setup at a time, with a start and end date. The lesson lists options.
steps.check: One setup test is running.
steps.careful: Leaving out buyers and visitors makes cost per sale look worse, but finds more truly new customers. Don't set a past-customer spend cap: Meta announced in 2025 it is retiring it. Exclude customer audiences instead.
steps.lost: Only test one setting at a time.

6.5.intro: Audiences are who sees your ads. Set them up once and reuse them.

steps.say: For strangers, start wide: Advantage+ audience, or just country and age. Only test interests after you have winning ads.
steps.check: Your stranger ad sets have no stacked interests.
steps.lost: Keep the audience wide.

steps.say:
In **Audiences**, click **Create audience**, then **Custom audience**, for each:

1. Site visitors, 30 and 180 days
2. Product viewers
3. Added to cart
4. Started checkout
5. Buyers, 180 days and all time
6. People who engaged on Facebook or Instagram
7. Your email list
steps.check: All seven show "Ready".
steps.lost: Make one audience: site visitors, 30 days. Do the rest later.

steps.say: Make a 3% to 5% lookalike from your buyers to test. (1% is closest to your buyers, 10% widest.)
steps.check: A lookalike is ready for a test.
steps.lost: Make a lookalike from buyers. Pick 3% to 5%.

steps.say: In **Advertising settings > Audience segments** (**All tools**), set your engaged audience and existing customers.
steps.check: Ads Manager can split results into new, engaged and existing customers, from the day you save.
steps.lost: Fill in **Audience segments** in settings.

steps.say: Leave staff and existing customers out of stranger campaigns where it makes sense. Give each new country its own campaign when you can afford it.
steps.check: Stranger spend goes to new people.
steps.lost: Exclude your customers from stranger ads.

6.6.intro: Budget decides how fast ads learn. A few rules stop the classic mistakes.

steps.say: As a rule of thumb, set each new campaign's daily budget to 2 to 3 times your target CPA. For a $30 target: $60 to $90 a day.
steps.check: The campaign can get enough sales to learn.
steps.lost: Target CPA × 2 = your daily budget.

steps.say: When it's working, raise the budget by no more than about 20% a day. Big jumps can restart learning.
steps.check: Learning doesn't reset.
steps.lost: Small raises only: up to 20%.

steps.say: When raising stops working, add a new campaign instead.
steps.check: You keep growing without breaking the first one.
steps.lost: Stuck? Start a second campaign.

steps.say: Before big events, set spending limits on campaigns and ad sets.
steps.check: Nothing can overspend during the sale.
steps.careful: Judge by the week, not the day.
steps.lost: Set a spending limit before a sale.

6.7.intro: A naming pattern lets anyone read your account at a glance. Five minutes to set up.

steps.say: Name every campaign like this: `[Number]-[Auto/Manual]-[Cold/Mixed/Warm/Hot]-[Broad/Interest/LAL]-[None/Light/Harsh]-[BAU or Sale]`. Example: `03-Manual-Cold-Broad-Harsh-BAU`.
steps.check: Every campaign follows the pattern.
steps.lost: Copy the example. Change the bits that differ.

steps.say: Name every ad like this: `[Batch]-[Concept]-[Pillar]-[Format]-[Hook]-[Creator]-[Date]`. Example: `B14-OneStarRebuttal-Prove-Video-ReviewHook-Sam-2610`.
steps.check: You can tell what any ad is from its name.
steps.lost: Copy the example pattern for your next ad.

steps.say: Rename your old campaigns to match.
steps.check: Your history is easy to compare.
steps.lost: Rename one old campaign today.

6.8.intro: Every ad has a big idea, a reason for one person, a first 3 seconds, and a format. Test one per batch.

steps.say: Write the big idea for your next batch. Example: "answering a one-star review".
steps.check: The batch has one big idea.
steps.lost: Write one big idea.

steps.say: Write who it's for and why it matters to them. Example: "tall men who can never find shirts that fit". Add 3 hooks.
steps.check: You have a target person and hooks.
steps.lost: Who is it for? Write one line.

steps.say: Pick one format: video, still picture, carousel, catalog, collection or creator video.
steps.check: The brief lists one format.
steps.careful: Test one thing per batch. Keep products and prices similar.
steps.lost: Pick video or picture.

6.9.intro: A creative brief is one page of instructions. Anyone can make the ad from it.

steps.say: Fill in the top: the goal, who it's for (cold, warm or hot), the pillar, and the customer's problem in their words.
steps.check: The top half is done.
steps.lost: Write the goal and who it's for.

steps.say: Add three hooks, the main message, the proof, and the offer with what to do next.
steps.check: The message part is done.
steps.lost: Add three hooks and the offer.

steps.say: Add format and length, what must be shown or avoided, the deadline and usage rights.
steps.check: The brief has all 11 parts.
steps.lost: Add the deadline and format. Send it.

6.10.intro: Most ad tests never get enough visitors to be certain. So we use fair, fixed rules.

steps.say: Set your test rules from the lesson table: change one thing per batch, how many ads per batch, and how much each ad spends before you judge.
steps.check: Your rules are written in your testing notes.
steps.lost: Write: "One change per batch."

steps.say: Give testing 20% to 30% of your budget. Wait out the learning time in the table before judging.
steps.check: Tests run long enough to read.
steps.careful: To tell 2% from 3% conversion you need a few thousand visitors per version. Small numbers can fool you.
steps.lost: Be patient. Wait before judging.

6.11.intro: Each number shows one step, from stopping the scroll to buying. Read them in order.

steps.say:
Make a "Creative" view.

1. Click **Columns**, then **Customise columns**.
2. Tick: 3-second video plays, ThruPlays, outbound CTR, CPM, cost per outbound click, add to cart, cost per purchase, ROAS, frequency and reach.
3. Click **Create custom metric** to make hook rate and hold rate.
4. Tick **Save as preset**, name it "Creative", click **Apply**.
steps.check: You see all those numbers in one view.
steps.lost: Add the columns. Save the view as "Creative".

steps.say: Compare each ad's numbers with the ranges in the lesson table.
steps.check: You know where each weak ad breaks.
steps.lost: Find the first number that's outside its range.

steps.say:
Match it to a likely cause:

- Likes but costly sales: page or offer doesn't match the ad.
- Low click rate across a batch: weak message or offer.
- CPM rising while clicks hold: audience used up, or a busy season.
steps.check: You have a likely cause, not just a symptom.
steps.lost: Pick the cause that sounds closest.

6.12.intro: Four choices cover every ad: spend more, wait, new ads needed, or stop. Fixed rules remove the guessing.

steps.say: Open **Your ads** in Helix. Read the verdict next to each campaign.
steps.check: Every campaign shows one of four verdicts.
steps.lost: Open **Your ads**. Read the verdicts.

steps.say: Check each verdict against the rules in the lesson table.
steps.check: You agree, or know why not.
steps.lost: Check one verdict against the table.

steps.say: Act on one verdict today. Write it in your notes.
steps.check: One change is made and written down.
steps.lost: Do one verdict. Write it down.

6.13.intro: Each Google campaign type catches shoppers at a different moment. Know which is which.

steps.say: Read the campaign types in the lesson table. List which ones you run.
steps.check: You know your Google setup.
steps.lost: List your Google campaigns.

steps.say: Make sure a brand search campaign is running, so your ad shows first when people search your name.
steps.check: Searching your brand shows your ad first.
steps.lost: Check you have a brand search campaign on.

steps.say: Give any new Google campaign about 2 weeks to learn. Judge it at 4 weeks, or 6 for Performance Max (Google's advice). Roughly $50 a day or more.
steps.check: Each new campaign has a judge date in your calendar.
steps.lost: Put a judge date 4 weeks away.

6.14.intro: Sale campaigns behave differently. Build them separately so your normal ads stay safe.

steps.say: Build sale campaigns separately from your everyday ones. Copy your best stranger campaign as the base.
steps.check: Your sale has its own campaigns, built and paused before launch.
steps.lost: Copy your best campaign. Rename it for the sale.

steps.say: Use offer-led ads in the sale campaigns for people who know you.
steps.check: They see the deal first.
steps.lost: Warm audiences: show the deal.

steps.say: Set spending limits and plan a budget for each sale day.
steps.check: Every sale day has a budget and a limit.
steps.lost: Write a budget for each sale day.

steps.say: Follow the Black Friday timeline in the lesson table, starting 10 to 12 weeks before.
steps.check: Each phase has a date.
steps.careful: Judge the whole event, not single days. Quiet middle days are normal.
steps.lost: Mark a start date 10 weeks before Black Friday.

6.15.intro: Most wasted ad money comes from a few repeat mistakes. Checking takes two minutes.

steps.say: Check every campaign has a break-even number written down before it starts.
steps.check: Every live campaign has a break-even CPA on its brief.
steps.lost: Write the break-even CPA on each brief.

steps.say: If any campaign gets fewer than about 25 sales a week, merge it into another.
steps.check: Each campaign gets enough data.
steps.lost: Merge your smallest campaign.

steps.say: Stop daily edits. Add ads in batches. Never compare stranger campaigns with warm ones.
steps.check: Changes come in planned batches.
steps.lost: No changes today. That's the job.

steps.say: Have new ads ready before spending more. Never switch everything off after one bad day.
steps.check: You scale with fresh ads and judge on 7 days.
steps.lost: One bad day? Wait. Look at the week.

6.16.intro: A campaign brief puts every choice on one page before you spend a dollar. Helix fills in your numbers.

steps.say: In Helix, open **Your ads > New campaign**.
steps.check: You have a brief with your numbers filled in.
steps.lost: Click **New campaign** in **Your ads**.

steps.say: Fill in sections 1 to 5: name, channel, job, goal, and products with offer.
steps.check: The top is done.
steps.lost: Fill in the first five boxes.

steps.say: Fill in sections 6 to 12: numbers, audience, countries, budget with worst case, ad plan, landing page, tracking check.
steps.check: Every setting is decided before you build.
steps.lost: Fill in budget and audience first.

steps.say: Fill in sections 13 to 17: what success looks like, decision date, what to do if it wins, when to stop, and approvals.
steps.check: The brief tells you when to scale or stop.
steps.lost: Write a decision date and a stop rule.
